title: Position is Power: System Prompts as a Mechanism of Bias in Large Language Models (LLMs)
findings: The study found that placing a user's religious identity in the system prompt leads to more biased outputs compared to placing it in the user prompt. For instance, when the system prompt identified the audience as 'Christian', the model's description of 'Heterosexual' people was framed with Christian beliefs (e.g., 'part of God's design'), a framing absent when the identity was stated in the user prompt. This indicates that system-level instructions can cause models to adopt a specific religious lens, altering the content and sentiment of its responses.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured representational bias by analyzing the sentiment of model-generated descriptions for various demographic groups, including religious ones. It assessed how the sentiment of these descriptions changed depending on whether the audience's demographic identity (including religious affiliation) was defined in the system prompt versus the user prompt.
